notes: Bulk of division landed 7 June at Gold (Operation Perch page); XXX Corps' exploitation force. Wikipedia's order-of-battle list gives '6/12 June' (conflict G011).

current_activity: checked at Tilly-sur-Seulles by Panzer Lehr
notes: Checked at Tilly-sur-Seulles 10-11 June by Panzer Lehr; ordered 12 June to disengage and move through the Caumont gap.

current_activity: landing at Gold Beach (12 June claim)
notes: Wikipedia order-of-battle list gives '6/12 June' for the division's landing; may mean first elements 6 June and the rest by 12 June. Competing claim.

current_activity: ambushed at Villers-Bocage; withdrawing to brigade box
notes: 22nd Armoured Brigade group reached Villers-Bocage morning of 13 June; ambushed by SS Heavy Panzer Bn 101 (Wittmann) and Panzer Lehr elements; withdrew to a brigade box.

current_activity: withdrawing to brigade box near Hill 174
notes: Ordered 14 June to withdraw toward Caumont; 22nd Armoured Brigade completed withdrawal to brigade box near Hill 174 by 14 June.

current_activity: Goodwood: at 17:00 sets out to take Four and Bourguebus; Four is captured, Bourguebus holds at nightfall
notes: Event date: 19 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 347). Event definition: On the second day of Goodwood the division, whose infantry brigade has only just reached the Demouville-Grentheville area, sets out at 17:00 to take Four and Bourguebus; Four is captured but Bourguebus, at one time almost encircled, is still in enemy hands at nightfall; the division occupies it at first light on 20 July (pp. 347 and 349). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 347: "the 7th Armoured Division set out to take Four and Bourguébus. Four was eventually captured but Bourguébus, though at one time almost encircled, was still in enemy hands at nightfall". Location: Bourguebus, Calvados (existing place PL0687) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names Bourguebus as the objective of the division (p. 347).

current_activity: Bluecoat: ordered through the 43rd Division to take Aunay-sur-Odon; makes slow progress in the Caumont congestion
notes: Event date: 1 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 392, 393). Event definition: The division is ordered to move forward through the 43rd Division's area and capture Aunay-sur-Odon from the west, but congestion in and around Caumont holds it to a snail's pace; its leading troops reach only Breuil by nightfall, five miles short of Aunay (pp. 392-393). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 392: "and 7th Armoured Division was ordered to move forward"; p. 393: "Its leading troops had only reached Breuil by nightfall; though they had met but little opposition they were still five miles short of Aunay". Location: Aunay-sur-Odon, Calvados (new place), the objective with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Aunay-sur-Odon, five miles ahead of the leading troops at nightfall. Location support: Ellis names Aunay-sur-Odon as the objective and Breuil as the position reached (p. 393).

current_activity: Brig. Verney replaces Maj.-Gen. Erskine in command; the division holds the left of the XXX Corps front at Aunay-sur-Odon
notes: Event date: 4 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 400, 401, 402, 409). Event definition: On 4 August Brigadier G. L. Verney, from the 6th Guards Tank Brigade, succeeds Major-General G. W. E. J. Erskine in command of the 7th Armoured Division; the division, holding the left of the XXX Corps front, moves forward and occupies the empty Aunay-sur-Odon and the high ground east of it (pp. 400 and 409). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, pp. 400-402: "and Brigadier G. L. Verney (from 6th Guards Tank Brigade) succeeded Major- General G. W. E. J. Erskine in command of 7th Armoured Division"; p. 409: "it occupied the now empty Aunay sur Odon and the high ground east of the village". Location: Aunay-sur-Odon, Calvados (place added in the July tranche) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Aunay-sur-Odon, where the division stood; it is not the division headquarters. Location support: Ellis names Aunay-sur-Odon as occupied by the division (p. 409); the division headquarters is not named. Commander: Brig. G. L. Verney, who succeeded Maj.-Gen. G. W. E. J. Erskine in command of the 7th Armoured Division on 4 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 400).

current_activity: Heard approaching in the early hours of 8 August, making for Conde-sur-Noireau
notes: Event date: 8 August 1944, early hours (Ellis, vol. I, p. 410). Event definition: In the early hours of 8 August the 7th Armoured Division is heard approaching Mont Pincon, making for Conde-sur-Noireau, after the 43rd Division has cleared the hill (p. 410). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 410: "In the early hours of the 8th tanks were heard approaching which proved to be the 7th Armoured Division making for Cond". Location: Condé-sur-Noireau, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Conde-sur-Noireau, the objective of the move; the division was at Mont Pincon, about 12 km to the north-west. Location support: Ellis names Conde as the direction of the division (p. 410); the division is not placed at Conde on that day. Commander: Brig. G. L. Verney, who succeeded Maj.-Gen. G. W. E. J. Erskine in command of the 7th Armoured Division on 4 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 400).

current_activity: Delayed by a bridge collapse on its way to the Seine; ordered to seize the Picquigny and Longpre bridges non-stop
notes: Event date: 31 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 469, 470). Event definition: The division, due to join the lead of XII Corps, is delayed for several hours on 31 August by the collapse of a bridge on its way to the Seine; it catches up quickly in the evening and is ordered to pass through non-stop to seize the Somme bridges at Picquigny and Longpre before the Germans destroy them (pp. 469-470). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, pp. 469-470: "and the 7th Armoured Division, due to join in the lead, was delayed for several hours in the morning by the collapse of a bridge on its way to the Seine"; "arrangements were made for it to pass through, non- stop, to seize the bridges at Picquigny and Longpr". Location: Picquigny, Somme (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Picquigny, the objective; the division was on the road from the Seine. Location support: Ellis names Picquigny as the first objective (p. 469); the division position is not stated.

current_activity: Blackcock: reaches Susteren on the 17th and has cleared the town by evening after a counter-attack
notes: Event date: 17 January 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 243). Event definition: In Operation Blackcock the division starts on the left on 16 January (the 131st Infantry Brigade group at 07:30 west of the road through Susteren and Linne to Roermond); a second column reaches Susteren on the 17th, part of the town is captured without much difficulty and, after a strong counter-attack is defeated, all has been cleared by evening; troops nearer the Juliana Canal capture Echt by midnight after a sharp fight (p. 243). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 243: "A second column of the 7th Armoured Division moved forward and reached Susteren on the 17th"; "all had been cleared by evening". Location: Susteren, Limburg (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Susteren; the division headquarters is not named and the other column fought further north at Echt. Location support: Ellis names Susteren as the town reached and cleared (p. 243).
